FIELD REFERENCE

Spotted bass: identification, size and seasonal trip tips

Spotted bass (Micropterus punctulatus), also called Kentucky bass, have rows of dark spots below the side stripe and a rough tongue patch. Missouri Conservation lists a usual length of 10–17 inches. For a fishing trip, match the water and season first, then check the local black bass rules before keeping fish.

Updated 2026-11-23 · Castward

What is a spotted bass, and how big does it get?

Key factDetail
Scientific nameMicropterus punctulatus
Other nameKentucky bass
Missouri size referenceUsually 10–17 inches and ½–3½ pounds (MDC)
Jaw checkReaches about the rear of the eye; largemouth jaw extends farther back
Body checkRows of spots below the main stripe
Fin checkDorsal fins connected; scales at the base of the second dorsal fin (FWC)
Florida minimum12 inches total length for spotted bass
Florida daily bag5 black bass combined; only one may be 16 inches or longer; local exceptions apply

How do you tell spotted bass from largemouth bass?

Start with the jaw and dorsal fins. FWC describes a spotted bass jaw that does not extend past the eye, connected dorsal fins and scales at the base of the second dorsal fin. The rough tongue patch is another clue. Compare the whole fish rather than one mark alone.

Read the source

When should you plan a spotted bass trip in Missouri?

MDC describes a spring move into smaller tributaries after high water, followed by a fall return to larger rivers and reservoirs. Dawn and dusk are active periods. Use that pattern to choose a trip type, then check current access and conditions; it does not predict a catch.

Read the source

What tackle can you use for spotted bass?

FWC lists jigs, crankbaits, spinners, small plastic worms and crayfish among the usual choices. Start with tackle you already own and match it to the water you will fish. If you book a guided day, ask which rods and lures are supplied before you buy more.

Read the source

What is the spotted bass size limit in Florida?

Florida’s general rule sets a 12-inch minimum total length for spotted bass. The daily bag is five black bass combined, with only one fish 16 inches or longer. Special waters have exceptions. Check the destination’s rule before you keep a fish, and measure total length rather than guessing.

Read the source

Where are spotted bass native in Texas?

TPWD places the native Texas range from the Guadalupe River to the Red River, excluding the Edwards Plateau. The agency highlights the Sabine, Neches and Cypress rivers. Use that range to narrow your search, then choose an actual access point and check the water’s current rules before travel.

Read the source

What should you know about spotted bass?

Is Kentucky bass another name for spotted bass?

Yes. Missouri Conservation lists Kentucky bass for Micropterus punctulatus.

How large are spotted bass?

MDC gives 10–17 inches as its usual length range. This regional guide is not a world-record claim.

Can spotted bass live in brackish water?

FWC says they do not enter brackish water. Choose a freshwater trip.

Are spotted bass always in rivers?

No. MDC also records them in large Ozark reservoirs.

Does Florida have a separate five-fish spotted bass bag?

No. Five is the combined black bass daily bag under the general rule. Local exceptions can apply.

Should I buy a new rod for a guided trip?

Ask what the guide supplies first. Match any purchase to the actual method and water.
